item.title: Transport Malta workers face pay cuts; union threatens to halt fines and clamping
item.description: At least 100 Transport Malta employees had overtime pay deducted this month after failing to clock in or out, with one worker reporting a cut of €1,600. The UĦM – Voice of the Workers registered an industrial dispute and gave the authority until noon on Monday 30 November to pay the amounts due. If the money is not paid, the union said enforcement officers will stop issuing traffic citations and clamping vehicles from 1 December, and that action could widen to other job grades.

item.title: Dalli says COP31 outcome was 'very disappointing' and hits out at oil industry lobbying
item.description: Environment, Energy and Regeneration Minister Miriam Dalli told parliament that the UN climate conference ended without a major agreement and that oil industry lobbying was among the obstacles. Citing the World Meteorological Organisation, she said the world has entered an era of climatic extremes with the Mediterranean a hotspot, and argued Malta is already seeing drought, water scarcity and longer heatwaves. She said climate spending accounts for 4% of total government expenditure, with 56% of the climate allocation going to adaptation and resilience, and defended electricity subsidies as necessary to keep energy prices affordable.

item.title: Audit report: 32 local councils given qualified opinions; 13 had negative working capital
item.description: The Auditor General's annual report on local government, presented to Speaker Carmelo Abela, found 32 of 53 councils received qualified audit opinions for 2025 for lack of supporting documentation, five were flagged over going-concern uncertainty, 13 recorded negative working capital and 18 a deficit. Mosta's negative working capital was the largest at €1,014,200, followed by Ħ'Attard (€706,966) and Qormi (€294,490).

item.title: Government to open call for Grand Harbour regeneration proposals
item.description: Energy Minister Miriam Dalli said the government is preparing a call for proposals to redevelop parts of Grand Harbour, following public consultation and expressions of interest from local and international investors. International consultants are assessing whether the redevelopment options are financially viable. She listed 2027 budget allocations of €400 million for energy subsidies, €212 million for energy infrastructure, €438 million for climate action and €63 million for greening projects, and said preparatory cleaning work has begun at Manoel Island.

item.title: PN questions €1.6 million allocation for animal aftercare clinic
item.description: Nationalist MPs argued during the Energy and Environment budget debate that funding for an animal aftercare clinic has been raised from €600,000 to €1.6 million while questions about the facility remain unanswered. MP Janice Abela Chetcuti said dozens of parliamentary questions on the matter have been deferred, while MP Andrew Agius asked whether the national animal hospital will run through a private concession and called for a public veterinary service in Gozo. Parliamentary Secretary Alicia Bugeja Said replied that the directorate's management structure is being strengthened.

item.title: ERA orders fish processing plant at Ħal Far to stop operating
item.description: The Environment and Resources Authority issued a suspension and compliance order on the fish by-products plant at Ħal Far after odour complaints were confirmed again in October, a problem reported since 2022. The plant must halt operations until an independent engineer verifies that its odour-reducing machinery is adequate and operating correctly. The Birżebbuġa local council has petitioned for the matter to be scrutinised in parliament.

item.title: 827 people registered as organ donors in first ten months of 2026
item.description: Health Minister Ian Borg told parliament that 827 people registered as organ donors between January and October 2026, compared with 587 for the whole of 2025, with 30,900 people on the donor register by end of October. Of the 2026 registrations, 538 were women, 288 men and one person was recorded under another gender category. The 2024 total was 1,373.

item.title: 31 people stopped receiving the Carer's Grant since 2021
item.description: Figures given to parliament by Social Policy and Family Minister Michael Falzon show 31 people stopped receiving the Carer's Grant since its introduction in January 2021, with 201 applications recorded up to September 2026. Stated reasons include the death of the beneficiary, payment moving from one parent to another, a child with severe disability entering an institution, or a review by the Professional Board lowering the disability level below the 75% threshold. Eligibility was extended in 2025 to parents of severely disabled children under 16.

item.title: Activists hold symbolic procession for female victims of violence
item.description: Moviment Graffitti organised a procession of mourning, remembrance and resistance in Republic Street, Valletta, to mark the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women. The event, titled "I am Jane Doe", focused on non-fatal violence against women whose cases go unreported. Participants wore white blood-stained dresses and carried candles, and speakers called for accessible, timely protection and specialised support services.

item.title: Christmas lights switched on in Valletta by 10-year-old transplant patient
item.description: Ellie Portelli, who had a successful liver transplant as a toddler, switched on the festive lights on Republic Street, with Culture Minister Malcolm Paul Agius Galea and Valletta Cultural Agency chairman Jason Micallef present. A Christmas tree near Parliament and the Nativity crib in St John's Square were also lit. The Valletta Cultural Agency is running a month of festivities, "Christmas in the Capital", ending with New Year's Eve in St George's Square.

item.title: PN asks who will be responsible for the new Malta in Motion agency
item.description: Shadow sustainable mobility minister Ivan Castillo said it is unclear who will be accountable for decisions once the proposed Malta in Motion agency is set up alongside Transport Malta and Infrastructure Malta. He noted the official plan gives rapid transit planning five years and construction a further ten, so the project could take 15 years to complete, and that the government has not presented an equivalent fallback if it is delayed or underfunded.

item.title: 27-year-old released on electronic monitoring over 56 sexual exploitation charges
item.description: Gian-Luke Gambin, who pleaded not guilty, was granted bail under an electronic monitoring order after being arrested in June on 56 charges involving alleged sexual exploitation and child grooming through fake social media profiles. Police identified at least nine alleged victims, seven of them minors, with the youngest aged 10. The case was triggered by an incident involving two sisters aged 10 and 12 and reports from other teenagers who contacted police.

item.title: Over 90% of Gozitans say they have faith in the Church and priests
item.description: A new Diocese of Gozo survey of 439 residents found 70.6% of respondents attend Sunday Mass, with 70% expecting religious life on the island to decline over the next decade. Attendance shows a clear generational gap: 83% of those over 55 attend Mass weekly, compared with 54.5% of those under 35 and 60.3% in the 35–54 age group. The survey was conducted by telephone between late June and mid-August 2026.

item.title: No VAT inspections took place in May, election month
item.description: Figures tabled in parliament by Finance Minister Clyde Caruana show VAT inspections fell from 653 in March to 26 in April and stopped entirely in May, the month of the general election. The reply, to a question by Nationalist MP Mark Anthony Sammut, gave no reason for the drop. Inspections resumed in June and reached 759 in September, the highest monthly figure in the report.
